task.title: Money Flow Wedge Scout
task.objective: Discover the strongest tiny programmable software/AI intervention inside an existing large private-sector money flow, continuously rank a best surviving hypothesis, attack it when all build gates appear satisfied, and persist every run so future runs continue from accumulated evidence rather than restarting.

operating_protocol.discovery_floor: Every run must return at least one best surviving hypothesis even if some gates remain uncertain.
freeze_build_threshold: recurring measurable leakage or unrealized value
credible tiny fee stronger than obvious self-serve or flat-fee alternatives
no need to own the core transaction or request path
no dominant or sufficiently close incumbent or first-party feature
operating_protocol.search_behavior: Before threshold maintain a current leader and try to beat it. At threshold enter ATTACK and search for disconfirming evidence. If it survives, freeze and build; if it fails, record fatal flaw and promote the next candidate.
operating_protocol.persistence_rule: Every scheduled or manual run must append its normalized result, candidate scores, gate changes, evidence, rejected reasons, current leader and next research test to Taskman persistence before completion.

conversation_history.summary: Opportunity search narrowed away from tenders, jobs, freelance lead hunting, buyer/seller matchmaking, manufacturer sourcing and generic demand creation toward programmable interventions in existing private money flows.
Adopted eight strict build gates and lifecycle SEARCH -> ATTACK -> FROZEN-BUILD.
Rejected after attack because trigger was customer-created, intervention sat on the request path, first-party cheaper lanes and gateways existed, and performance pricing was weak.
Added two-level standard: every run must return a best surviving hypothesis while final build threshold stays strict; search breadth widened and now drills flow -> state transition -> micro-decision.
Clean authorization/fulfillment/expiry trigger, later weakened by first-party capture/reauthorization features and payment orchestration.
Strong minimum-spend shortfall economics, later weakened by cloud commitment managers and procurement/SaaS allocation tooling.
Excellent economics but current systems reconcile volume commitments, deficiency payments and make-up rights.
Promising pattern: two legitimate future uses already exist and a contractual or quota state changes which is economically optimal; detect before the decision and redirect existing activity.
Prepaid messaging credits plus scheduled sends created a good trigger; later search found mature multi-provider SMS routing/cost optimization layers.
GitHub/Taskman selected as permanent anchor for search state, evidence, rejected paths, scores, task results and conversation-derived knowledge.
Every recurring research run must read Taskman first and persist the full normalized result back to Taskman before completion.
Included/prepaid SaaS or API capacity approaching a reset with deferrable work remains a strong mechanism, but this run found a cleaner named vertical in synthetic monitoring.

Provider-native app-store grace windows create a real net-margin choice for high-variable-cost apps, but the decision is app-wide/infrequent, relatively spreadsheetable and difficult to attribute for performance pricing.
Refund-promise to settlement matching remains attractive, but enterprise reconciliation products already surface missing refunds and aggregate leakage remains unquantified.
Exact tools already identify unused labels and automate carrier refunds/voids.

conversation_history.candidate: Prior-authorization expiry before scheduled service watchdog
conversation_history.summary: Current authorization tools already track expiry and flag authorizations that will expire before scheduled procedures.
Material idle-cash loss exists but treasury/bank-fee tools and bank sweeps already optimize the exact state.
Dedicated software already tracks refundable core deposits, deadlines, returns and credits.
Corporate travel software already auto-cancels to avoid no-show fees and lost value.

conversation_history.candidate: Vendor credit memo application before payment
conversation_history.summary: ERP/AP tools already track and apply unapplied vendor credits.
Quota-boundary opportunities are strongest when the financial unit and work unit are independently machine-readable and the action can be timing rather than routing through our infrastructure.

Synthetic monitoring exposes a direct billable event, independently generated schedules and usage records, and APIs that can change frequency/downtime. The proposed wedge continuously adapts test frequency to traffic, deployment, incident and SLO state while measuring avoided check spend. Exact adaptive-cost competition was not found in this run; Gate 8 and savings magnitude remain uncertain.

current_leader.name: Adaptive synthetic-monitor frequency optimizer
current_leader.state_transition: fixed synthetic-check schedule -> traffic/deployment/incident/risk state changes -> fixed frequency becomes unnecessarily expensive or insufficiently protective -> change test frequency/downtime through provider API -> preserve required detection coverage with fewer billable checks -> verified monitoring spend avoided
current_leader.why_survived: New Relic currently exposes finite included synthetic checks and charges for additional checks, while monitor frequency multiplied by locations determines monthly check count. New Relic and Datadog expose APIs and usage metrics that allow a sidecar to read cost state and modify frequency/downtime without proxying application requests. Fresh searches found static usage dashboards, alerts, budgets and manual interval-tuning guidance but no sufficiently close product whose narrow job is continuously adapting synthetic-test frequency to changing operational risk while measuring avoided check spend.
strongest_evidence: New Relic pricing currently includes 500 synthetic checks on Free and prices additional synthetics checks beyond included amounts at $0.005/check.
New Relic docs show frequency and selected locations directly determine monthly check count; three locations at 15-minute frequency yields 8,640 checks/month.
New Relic APIs can create/update synthetic monitors and scheduled downtimes; Datadog exposes estimated synthetic usage metrics and programmable downtimes.
Current cost-optimization guidance identifies interval and multi-region frequency as major multiplicative cost drivers, but this run did not find an exact adaptive-frequency FinOps product.
current_leader.closest_threat: Observability vendors already provide usage alerts, static budgets, configurable frequencies and downtimes; existing observability FinOps tools may evolve to mutate schedules. The wedge dies if manual static configuration captures most savings or if automatic adaptive scheduling already exists at scale.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read monitor definitions, historical run counts, traffic/service criticality, deployment calendars, incident state and SLO constraints; compute a minimum-safe frequency per monitor; recommend frequency/downtime changes first, then optionally write them through provider APIs. Maintain a counterfactual ledger of baseline planned checks versus optimized checks and detected incidents.
current_leader.monetization: Small fee per optimized monitor-month or capped percentage of verified avoided billable checks, counted only while reliability/SLO guardrails remain satisfied.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: Need to prove material enterprise overspend and demonstrate that dynamic frequency reduction saves meaningful dollars without degrading detection latency, contractual monitoring requirements or compliance coverage.
current_leader.next_research_test: ATTACK-LIKE SEARCH while remaining SEARCH mode: find exact observability FinOps products that automatically mutate synthetic-test frequency; model annual savings for 100-1000 API/browser monitors across multiple regions; verify update permissions and operational guardrails across New Relic and Datadog. Kill if typical savings are sub-$1k/year or first-party adaptive scheduling already exists.

runner_ups.reason: General mechanism remains strong, but synthetic monitoring is a cleaner vertical with explicit billable events, usage metrics and write APIs.
Excellent attribution but unquantified leakage and closer reconciliation competition.
Real economics but infrequent app-wide control and weaker performance attribution.

new_search_rules: A quota vertical is stronger when the provider charges explicitly per billable event and exposes both usage and configuration APIs.
Prefer adjustable recurring machine schedules over one-time settings because they create repeated monetizable decisions and stronger attribution.
For operational-safety wedges, savings must be conditional on a non-financial guardrail such as SLO, detection latency or compliance coverage.

A static first-party budget or usage dashboard is an adjacent threat but not an exact Gate-8 killer if the proposed layer automatically changes future event frequency using independent operational state.
